Saved a new reference `continuously-compounded-growth-rate.md` plus a SKILL.md pointer, capturing two generalizable points for future Treasury Bulletin questions:

1. "Continuously compounded average annual growth rate" = ln(V_end/V_start)/n — NOT CAGR ((ratio)^(1/n)−1). The word "continuously" flips the formula, and the two diverge enough to change the thousandths digit.
2. n = end_year − start_year (the time span). "End of CY 1945 to 1955" → n=10, not 11 and not a count of labels.

No memory entry needed — the reference file plus pointer covers it without bloating the near-full memory store.
